functional_semantics.triton: hist[b] = number of input values equal to b for b in [0, num_bins); values outside the range are dropped by the valid mask (impl_triton.py L39-42); output (num_bins,) int32 (L124).
functional_semantics.cutile: Same: out-of-range values contribute an update of 0 (impl_cutile.py L56-62); output (num_bins,) int32 (L107).
functional_semantics.note: Both match impl_torch.py L9 (bincount(minlength=num_bins).to(int32)) for in-range inputs; the generator produces arange(N) % num_bins (tensors.py L554-556), so every value is in range and the exact (atol = rtol = 0) check holds. torch would raise on negatives / grow the output for values >= num_bins; neither manual side does, and the contract makes out-of-range handling 'must not corrupt in-range counts'.

stages.triton: s0: histogram = torch.empty, partial = torch.zeros((num_partials, num_bins), int32) inside run() (L124-128); s1: partial kernel, grid (num_partials,), program p owns row p and grid-strides over the input in chunks (L31-42); s2: reduce kernel, per bin slice sums the partial rows in row chunks with tl.sum(axis=0) and stores (L56-70); launched s1 then s2 on the same stream (L141-155).
stages.cutile: s0: histogram = torch.empty, partial = torch.zeros inside run() (L107, L116); s1: partial kernel, grid (num_partials, 1, 1), program pid owns row pid and grid-strides over chunks (L45-64); s2: reduce kernel per bin slice with ct.sum(axis=0) over row tiles (L76-90); launched s1 then s2 (L142-145, L169-173).
stages.note: Identical three-step structure (zero-filled global scratch of private rows -> private counting -> column-sum reduce). NOT a register/shared-memory histogram primitive on either side: both count with global-memory atomic adds into the program's own row (L42 / L64). num_partials = min(cap, ceil(N / default chunk)) on both sides (L127 / L113).

dependencies.triton: s1 requires the zeroed scratch (atomic accumulation); s2 requires every s1 program to have finished (separate launch on the same stream); no two s1 programs write the same row.
dependencies.cutile: Same (zeroed scratch L116, two launches L142/L169, private rows L60).
dependencies.note: Identical dependency graph; a single-launch fusion would need a grid-wide barrier, which neither side uses.

reduction_scan_sort.triton: s1: tl.atomic_add of a vector of ones MASKED to valid lanes (L32, L42), so invalid/tail lanes issue no atomic; s2: sequential loop over BLOCK_ROWS-row chunks with an intra-chunk tl.sum tree (L61-68).
reduction_scan_sort.cutile: s1: ct.atomic_add of an int32 update that is 1 for valid lanes and 0 for invalid lanes, with invalid lanes redirected to bin 0 (L60-64); s2: sequential loop over row tiles with ct.sum (L80-88).
reduction_scan_sort.note: Both are order-free exact int32 counting followed by an exact column sum; masking the atomic versus adding 0 is a mapping choice with identical counts. No sort, no scan.

precision.note: Exact integer arithmetic; result independent of scheduling.

preprocessing.triton: input.contiguous() (L123, no-op); output allocation (L124); num_partials from the default chunk size (L118, L127); partial scratch allocated AND zero-filled with torch.zeros on every call (L128).
preprocessing.cutile: input.contiguous() (L106, no-op); output allocation (L107); num_partials (L110-113); partial scratch torch.zeros every call (L116); autotune-only throwaway scratch (L124) outside the default path.
preprocessing.note: Identical: the scratch memset (num_partials * num_bins * 4 bytes) is inside the timed run() on both sides and is required by the atomic accumulation; nothing is cached across calls.

intermediate_storage.triton: partial: (num_partials, num_bins) int32 global scratch, zeroed per call, written by s1 with atomics, read by s2, released after run() (L128).
intermediate_storage.note: Both agree on a global scratch of private partial rows; its size is bounded by the partial cap times num_bins and does not scale with N.

mutation.triton: No input written; fresh scratch and output per call (L124, L128).
mutation.cutile: No input written; fresh scratch and output per call (L107, L116).
mutation.note: Idempotent; contract forbids input mutation and cross-call scratch reuse.

fq_boundary.note: dtype_size = 4. The formula counts one read of the N int32 inputs and one write of the num_bins int32 output only. The timed run() on BOTH sides additionally (i) zero-fills the (num_partials, num_bins) int32 scratch with torch.zeros (impl_triton.py L128 / impl_cutile.py L116), (ii) performs N atomic read-modify-writes into that scratch, and (iii) reads the whole scratch back in the reduce kernel; none of this is in bytes_expr. For the small-N / large-num_bins corner of the sweep (N = 262144, num_bins = 4096, 256 partials) the scratch is 4 MiB versus a 1 MiB input, so reported bandwidth there is a lower bound on actual traffic. No prepacked input or cached state exists; the mismatch is an uncounted in-run zero-fill/scratch, not an untimed prepack.

review_items: (non-blocking, metric) bytes_expr omits the per-call scratch zero-fill (num_partials * num_bins * 4 B memset inside run()), the N atomic read-modify-writes into the scratch and the reduce pass's full scratch read, all of which are inside the timed window on both sides: decide whether to keep the compulsory-traffic convention (input read + output write) or to add the scratch traffic so that bandwidth/SOL figures are not understated in the small-N / large-num_bins corner.

(non-blocking, scope) Both implementations count with global-memory atomic adds into a private row of a zero-filled global scratch; the contract requires the two-level structure (private partial histograms, then a cross-partial sum) and a scratch initialised inside run(), but leaves the private-row update mechanism (per-element atomics versus on-chip pre-aggregation such as a register/shared-memory histogram primitive followed by additive updates of the row) as a permitted mapping. Confirm that this freedom is intended, since on-chip pre-aggregation can cut the scratch traffic the manual kernels pay.
